question: In which year did the Central Government merge the CSO and NSSO and establish NSO under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI)?
solution:
The correct answer is __**2019**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Central Government merged the Central Statistics Office (CSO) and the National Sample Survey Office (NSSO) in **2019**.
 
• This merger led to the creation of the **National Statistical Office (NSO)**, which now operates under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI).
 
• The primary goal of this restructuring was to streamline data collection, processing, and dissemination while improving transparency and efficiency.
 
• The NSO acts as the apex body for coordinating statistical activities across the country and ensuring the reliability of national data.
 
• This move was part of the government's broader initiative to modernize and strengthen India's statistical system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Central Statistics Office (CSO):**

 
 
• CSO was responsible for coordinating statistical activities and maintaining statistical standards across India.
 
• It primarily focused on compiling national accounts, price statistics, and socio-economic indicators.
 
 
 
• **National Sample Survey Office (NSSO):**
 
 
• NSSO was established in 1950 to conduct large-scale surveys on socio-economic indicators like employment, consumption, and health.
 
• It played a critical role in providing data for policymaking and development planning in India.
 
 
 
• **National Statistical Office (NSO):**
 
 
• NSO is the unified body resulting from the merger of CSO and NSSO.
 
• It is tasked with conducting surveys, compiling statistics, and releasing critical data on various socio-economic aspects.
 
• NSO also works to ensure the quality, reliability, and timeliness of official statistics.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI):**
 
 
• MoSPI oversees the functioning of NSO and is responsible for framing policies, standards, and methodologies for statistical activities.
 
• The ministry plays a vital role in ensuring data-driven policymaking in the country.
